documents.content:
### Section 5.05. Duties of Members.

Each member shall:

(a) Comply with these Bylaws, the policies of the Board, and the decisions of the members at any properly convened meeting;

(b) Pay all fees, dues, levies, and charges lawfully imposed by the Board or by the members in accordance with these Bylaws;

(c) Deliver to the cooperative, at the time and place directed by the Board, all produce, grain, or other commodities that the member has agreed to deliver under any contract or marketing agreement entered into with the cooperative;

(d) Give prompt notice to the Secretary of any change in the member's name, address, or other contact information, as required by Section 5.03;

(e) Use the cooperative's facilities, services, and marketing channels in a manner that does not endanger the safety of other members, employees, or the public; and

(f) Refrain from any conduct that brings the cooperative into disrepute or that is inconsistent with the cooperative's purposes and the common interest of its members.

### Section 5.06. Termination of Membership.

Membership in the cooperative shall terminate upon any of the following events:

(a) Voluntary resignation. A member may resign by delivering a written notice of resignation to the Secretary. Resignation shall be effective upon receipt of the notice, unless a later effective date is specified in the notice.

(b) Expulsion. The Board may, by a two-thirds vote of all Board members, expel a member for:
   (i) Failure to pay any dues, fees, or charges within sixty days after the same become due, provided the member has been given written notice of the delinquency and an opportunity to be heard before the Board;
   (ii) Repeated or serious violation of these Bylaws or of any Board policy, after written notice and an opportunity to be heard;
   (iii) Conduct that is materially harmful to the cooperative, its property, or its business relationships; or
   (iv) Conviction of a crime involving fraud, theft, or other dishonesty in connection with the cooperative's affairs.

(c) Death or dissolution of the member.

(d) Termination of the member's eligibility under Section 5.01.

Upon termination, the former member shall remain liable to the cooperative for all debts, deliveries, and obligations accrued before the effective date of termination. The Board may, in its discretion, withhold payment of any patronage dividend or other distribution otherwise payable to the former member until all such obligations are satisfied.

A former member whose membership was terminated for a reason other than expulsion may reapply for membership in accordance with Section 5.02. A former member expelled under subsection (b) may not reapply for a period of two years from the date of expulsion, unless the Board, by a two-thirds vote, waives this restriction.

### Section 5.07. Transfer of Membership.

Membership in the cooperative is personal to the member and shall not be transferable or assignable, except that upon the death of a member, the cooperative may, in its discretion, recognize the deceased member's spouse, child, or other designated beneficiary as a member if such person meets the eligibility requirements of Section 5.01 and agrees in writing to be bound by these Bylaws. Any such recognition shall be effective only upon approval by the Board.

## ARTICLE VI. MEETINGS OF MEMBERS

### Section 6.01. Annual Meeting.

The annual meeting of the members shall be held at such time and place, within the cooperative's area of operation, as the Board shall determine, and shall be held not later than the end of the cooperative's fiscal year. At the annual meeting, the members shall elect directors and officers, receive reports on the cooperative's affairs, and transact such other business as may properly come before the meeting.

### Section 6.02. Special Meetings.

Special meetings of the members may be called by the President, by the Board, or by the Secretary upon the written request of at least ten percent of the members entitled to vote. The request shall state the purpose or purposes of the proposed special meeting. No business other than that stated in the notice of a special meeting may be transacted at that meeting.

1.0 READING AND CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES OF PREVIOUS MEETING

The minutes of the meeting held on Saturday, 21st January 2023, were read by the Acting Secretary, Amina Bello, and circulated to all members present.

Matters arising from the minutes were discussed under Item 2.0.

The minutes were confirmed as a true record of the proceedings of that meeting, subject to the observations noted below.

Motion for confirmation: Proposed by Alhaji Bello Yusuf, seconded by Mrs. Grace Adeyemi. Carried unanimously.

---

2.0 MATTERS ARISING

2.1 Loan recovery drive (Action from January meeting): The Treasurer reported that the recovery drive for outstanding member loans has been progressing, but 12 out of 47 defaulters have still not made any payment. The Chairman directed that a final warning letter be issued to these members, giving them 21 days to pay or face suspension of their cooperative privileges. Action: Treasurer to draft letters by 25th April 2023.

According to the Board Meeting Minutes, Amina Bello's appointment_date was set as 2023-04-15. Record status: current.

2.2 Construction of the new warehouse: The Chairman reported that the contractor, Messrs. Gidan Dambe Construction, has completed the foundation and is now working on the walls. The project is on schedule for completion by August 2023. The Board noted the progress with satisfaction.

2.3 Death of a member: The Board noted with sadness the passing of Alhaji Musa Sule, a long-standing member of the cooperative. A condolence visit was made in February. The family has indicated they will continue the membership through his son, Mallam Abubakar Sule. This will be formalized at the next general meeting.

---

3.0 REPORT OF THE TREASURER (FINANCIAL REPORT FOR Q1 2023)

The Treasurer, Alhaji Musa Ibrahim, presented the financial report for the first quarter of 2023 (January – March). The report was circulated in writing. Key points:

- Total income for Q1: ₦18,450,000 (including member contributions, interest on loans, and proceeds from the sale of farm inputs)
- Total expenditure: ₦12,780,000 (including staff salaries, administrative costs, and payment for the first phase of the warehouse construction)
- Net surplus for the quarter: ₦5,670,000
- Outstanding loans to members (principal + interest): ₦3,250,000
- Cash at bank (as at 31st March 2023): ₦9,400,000 (Union Bank, Kano main branch, Account No. 2013456789)

The Treasurer noted that the surplus is higher than projected due to increased sales of fertilizer and improved seed during the early planting season. He recommended that the Board consider setting aside a portion of the surplus for the cooperative's reserve fund, as required by the by-laws.

Discussion: Mrs. Grace Adeyemi asked about the high administrative costs. The Treasurer explained that these included a one-off payment for the renovation of the office roof, which was completed in February. The Vice Chairman suggested that future renovation costs be budgeted separately to avoid distorting quarterly comparisons. This was agreed.

Resolution: The Board approved the financial report and directed that 20% of the Q1 surplus (₦1,134,000) be transferred to the reserve fund. The remaining surplus is to be retained for the fertilizer procurement program (see Item 6.0).

Motion: Proposed by Alhaji Musa Ibrahim, seconded by Mr. Daniel Eze. Carried unanimously.

- Total income for Q1: ₦24,780,000 (including member contributions, interest on loans, and proceeds from the sale of farm inputs)
- Total expenditure: ₦16,450,000 (including staff salaries, administrative costs, and the first phase of the warehouse construction)

The Treasurer noted that the surplus is higher than in the same period last year, driven by increased sales of fertilizer and improved seed during the early planting season. He recommended that the Board consider setting aside a portion of the surplus for the cooperative’s reserve fund, as required by the by-laws.

The Treasurer explained that these included a one-off payment for the purchase of a new computer and printer for the office, which was necessary for the digitalization of records. Mr. Peter Okonkwo suggested that future equipment purchases be budgeted separately. This was agreed.

**4.0 REPORT OF THE CHAIRMAN ON THE STATE-LEVEL COOPERATIVE SUMMIT**

The Chairman, Alhaji Sani Abdullahi, reported on the State-Level Cooperative Summit held in Kano on 15 May 2024. He highlighted the following points:

- The State Government has announced a new subsidy program for fertilizer purchases, effective from the 2024 planting season. The subsidy is available to registered cooperatives.
- The cooperative has been pre-qualified for the subsidy, subject to submission of the 2023 audited accounts and a list of active members.
- The Chairman noted that the subsidy will reduce the cost of fertilizer by approximately 15% for the upcoming season.
- The summit also discussed the importance of early planning for the harvest season, including storage and logistics.

documents.title: Board Meeting Minutes
documents.content:
**5.0 FERTILIZER PROCUREMENT PROGRAM – 2024 PLANTING SEASON**

The Board reviewed the report of the Fertilizer Procurement Committee, presented by its chairman, Alhaji Musa Ibrahim. The Committee had been tasked with sourcing fertilizer for the 2024 planting season, taking advantage of the subsidy programme announced at the State-Level Cooperative Summit.

**Discussion:** Mr. Daniel Eze noted that the subsidy application requires the 2023 audited accounts and the list of active members. He confirmed that both documents had been submitted to the State Ministry of Agriculture on 3 June 2024, and that a copy of the submission acknowledgment was available in the cooperative’s file. The Chairman commended Mr. Eze for the timely submission.

The Committee reported that, based on the subsidy, the estimated cost of NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer would be ₦19,000 per bag, down from the market rate of approximately ₦22,500. The cooperative intends to purchase 1,200 bags: 800 bags of NPK 15-15-15 and 400 bags of Urea. The total estimated cost, after subsidy, is ₦21,600,000 for NPK and ₦8,800,000 for Urea, giving a combined total of ₦30,400,000.

Mrs. Grace Adeyemi enquired about the delivery schedule. The Committee stated that the supplier, Kano Agro-Chemicals Ltd., has committed to delivering the first consignment of 600 bags by 10 July 2024, with the balance to be delivered in two batches before the end of August 2024. Payment terms are 50% on order and 50% on delivery of the final batch. The Board approved the payment of the initial 50% deposit, amounting to ₦15,200,000, from the retained surplus referred to in Item 3.0.

**Resolution:** The Board approved the fertilizer procurement plan as presented, and authorised the Chairman to sign the purchase agreement with Kano Agro-Chemicals Ltd. The Treasurer was directed to arrange the deposit payment before 28 June 2024.

Motion: Proposed by Mr. Peter Okonkwo, seconded by Mrs. Grace Adeyemi. Carried unanimously.

---

**6.0 HARVEST SEASON 2024 PLANNING**

The Board discussed the preliminary plans for the 2024 harvest season. The Chairman reminded members that the harvest season is expected to commence on 1 October 2024, and that early planning is essential to avoid the storage and logistics problems experienced in previous years.

**Discussion:** The following points were raised:

- The Storage Committee, chaired by Mr. Daniel Eze, reported that the cooperative’s main warehouse at the Danbatta Road facility has a capacity of 3,000 metric tonnes. A preliminary inspection in May 2024 found the warehouse to be in good condition, but the roof requires minor repairs before the onset of the rains. The Board directed that the repairs be undertaken in July 2024, at an estimated cost of ₦450,000.
- The Marketing Committee proposed that the cooperative begin identifying buyers for the expected harvest in advance. A preliminary enquiry has been received from a grain merchant in Kaduna, who has expressed interest in purchasing up to 1,500 metric tonnes of maize at prevailing market rates. No agreement has been signed.
- The Chairman noted that the cooperative should also make provision for the transport of produce from member farms to the warehouse. In previous seasons, the cooperative has hired trucks from private operators. The Board agreed that the Transport Sub-Committee should obtain quotations from at least three transporters and present them at the next Board meeting.

The Board noted the importance of completing the roof repairs and securing transport arrangements before the end of September 2024. The Treasurer was asked to include the estimated costs for these items in the revised budget for the second half of the year, to be presented at the next meeting.

---

**7.0 MEMBERSHIP AND WELFARE COMMITTEE UPDATE**

Mrs. Grace Adeyemi, chairperson of the Membership and Welfare Committee, reported on the committee’s activities since the last meeting. The committee has processed 23 new membership applications during the quarter. Of these, 21 met the eligibility criteria and were recommended for approval; the remaining 2 applications were deferred pending clarification of the applicants’ farm locations. The Board approved the 21 new members, bringing the total active membership to 312 as of the end of May 2024.
